title: Enterprise fast-path intake and safe-sandbox for third-party model onboarding
creator: Aisha Cohen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers occasionally request rapid addition of third-party or open-source models (new weights / forks / versions) for pilot projects. Current catalog intake is thorough but slow; enterprise buyers want a predictable, auditable fast-path that preserves safety and rollback controls while delivering the model to a sandbox that mirrors production.

Goal: Define and operationalize an 'Enterprise Fast-Path' intake lane that allows sponsored enterprise requests to reach a secure sandbox within 7 business days for evaluation, with automated gating for core safety, performance, and compliance checks. The lane should integrate with the model catalog so that any promotion to production still requires full evals and a pinning/rollback plan.

Scope: Non-bug product ticket for model catalog onboarding (new model adds, initial version pins, and temporary shadowing for deprecations). Excludes long-term custom infra work and performance kernel rewrites. Includes: intake form changes, triage rubric, sandbox provisioning template, automated smoke-eval pipeline, and documentation for sponsor approvals.

Triage rubric highlights (fast-path thresholds):
- First-touch triage window: 72 hours.
- Sponsor required: enterprise customer sponsor + technical steward.
- Data sensitivity check: If model training data is PII-sensitive or customer-supplied secrets involved => route to full private onboarding (not fast-path).
- Performance quick checks (on equivalent hardware): p50 generation latency <= 200ms for short prompts (<=32 tokens) and p95 <= 800ms; throughput baseline measured in tokens/sec; model memory <= 32GB for single-GPU fast-path variants.
- Safety quick-checks: toxicity and instruction-following smoke tests (automated suite), hallucination score <= 0.15 on curated prompt set for initial pass.
- Compatibility checks: supports KV-cache semantics or compatible variant; quantization-friendly checkpoint available (4-bit or 8-bit) OR engineering approval for unquantized path.
- Licensing & legal: SPDX-compatible license check OR signed enterprise agreement acknowledging license trade-offs.

Fast-path outputs:
- Temporary catalog entry flagged "enterprise-fast-path" with shadow-pin metadata (owner, sponsor, expiry)
- Sandbox deployed with observability hooks (latency, token-cost, error-rate) surfaced in Console pre-populated dashboard link
- Automated smoke-eval results attached and summarized in ticket
- Defined rollback and deprecation window (default 30 days for fast-path sandbox; production pin requires formal rollout)

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket):
1) Intake form additions live in Console and internal request portal.
2) Automated triage runner (scripts + checklist) can classify a request as fast-path or full-onboard with loggable reason codes.
3) Sandbox provisioning template with standard IAM/KMS placeholders and observability dashboard URL is generated automatically.
4) Smoke-eval pipeline runs end-to-end for a submitted model and writes a results summary (toxicity, basic hallucination metric, latency percentiles) into the ticket.
5) Playbook for sponsor approvals and escalation path documented in Confluence with at least one enterprise pilot identified.
6) Security sign-off flow hooked when security_review_required is true.

Risks & open questions:
- Fast-path could increase operational surface area and accidental production promotion; mitigate with hard expiration and promotion guardrails.
- Some enterprise models may require on-prem/VPC-only paths; we need a clear auto-escalation.
- Quantized variants may not exist for emergent open checkpoints; engineering effort to create safe quantized artifacts may be nontrivial.

Next steps:
- Sync w/ ENG owners (runtime + infra) to agree on smoke-eval definitions and the minimum hardware spec for fast-path.
- Design to mock the intake form changes and sponsor flow.
- Legal to review license template language.
- Identify pilot customer and schedule a 30-min intake dry-run.
